validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + DUPLICATE (this row's live orchestrator flag was: is P5927 the same physical pipe as P5928, double-counted?): INVESTIGATED AND REFUTED with strong independent evidence -- there genuinely are TWO separate parallel physical lines, not one line entered twice. (1) A 2020-vintage pre-design/EIA document for the THIRD (new) branch pipeline, filed with Kazakhstan's environmental portal ecoportal.kz ('Пояснительная записка', project 113/2020-12-03-ОПЗ), states the new line's route runs 'в одном техническом коридоре с существующими 2-мя нитками газопроводов-отводов «КС-14 город Актобе»' (in one technical corridor with the EXISTING TWO STRINGS of the 'CS-14 -- Aktobe city' gas pipeline laterals) up to km123, then alongside '...существующих 2-х ниток газопроводов-отводов Dн 530 мм' up to km136 -- explicitly TWO strings, explicitly Dн(outer)=530mm, explicitly named 'CS14-Aktobe'. The same document lists BOTH '1 нитка МГ «Газопровод-отвода г.Актобе»' and '2 нитка МГ «Газопровод-отвод на г.Актобе»' as SEPARATE line items across the chainage segments 26-86km, 86-110km, 110-134km and 134-136km -- two separately itemized strings running the same corridor, which is what supports the refutation. CORRECTION (Leg 3, 2026-08-11): our earlier reading of the 158,573 figure in that table as an itemized 158.573 km LENGTH for each string is WITHDRAWN. The table is headed 'Объем стравленного газа, тыс.м3' -- gas blown down during a shutdown, in thousand m3 -- and the same 158,573 recurs identically across DIFFERENT chainage segments, which no cumulative length could. So GEM's 158.00 km is NOT corroborated by this document; the two-strings finding does not depend on it, and the document's own length-bearing text puts the two strings parallel from km26 to ~km134-136 with a final single ~22 km leg to GRS-1. (2) Independently, a July 2023 news report (Aktobe Times, quoting the regional governor's office at a groundbreaking ceremony for the NEW third line) states 'минувшей зимой две существующие нитки были загружены на 170%' (last winter the two EXISTING lines were loaded at 170% of capacity) and separately gives the new third line's own specs (165 km, 2.4 bcm/y) which independently match this same pipeline family's GEM entry for 'CS 14-Aktobe III' exactly -- corroborating that whoever is tracking this system (GEM's own wiki editors, independently) is using consistent, verifiable figures, which increases confidence in the parallel figures for lines I/II too. Two independent origins (a technical EIA/design filing and a government-sourced news report, different authors, different years, different purposes) both explicitly describe TWO existing physical strings -- this is not a bibliographic double-count. CLASSIFICATION: correct as transmission/trunk gas pipeline carrying natural gas -- both documents describe it as a 'магистральный газопровод-отвод' (trunk gas pipeline lateral/branch) carrying 'природного газа' (natural gas), not a gathering or process line. DIAMETER RECONCILIATION NOTE (not a defect): the OTHER existing ref already on this row (the 2022 gov.kz public-hearing PDF, cited for Length) describes the SAME lateral with 'D - 500 мм' rather than 530mm. This is not a contradiction: Russian pipeline convention distinguishes Dу (условный проход/nominal bore, ~internal) from Dн (наружный диаметр/outer diameter) -- a Dу500 steel pipe has a standard outer diameter of Dн530, so '500mm' and '530mm' most likely describe the identical physical pipe under the two different diameter conventions, not two different diameters. GEM's Diameter=530 matches the ecoportal.kz document's explicit 'Dн 530 мм' (outer diameter, the convention GEM normally records), so no change recommended. GULFPUB CROSSWALK NOTE: GulfPub's matched value for this line, 'Krasnooktyabrskaya - Aktobe' at 135.19 km, is very likely NOT a shorter measurement of the full lateral but a measurement to an intermediate waypoint -- the 2022 gov.kz PDF places 'ГРС-2 г. Актобе' (Aktobe gas-distribution station 2) at exactly km135 of this same lateral, well short of its full ~158.6 km run to GRS-1/the city terminus. GulfPub (Tier 2, single source) is not treated as overriding the two-source 158/158.573 km corroboration above. CAPACITY CAVEAT: could not independently confirm 1.96 bcm/y (nor the wiki's stated 3.92 bcm/y combined total for both lines) against a primary source giving that exact figure in bcm/y -- the existing sheet ref (a gov.kz news page) is a client-rendered JavaScript SPA stub (200 OK but body is only 777 chars of app shell, no article text reachable without a browser) and could not be read even by direct fetch of likely API endpoints. The ecoportal.kz EIA document's own hydraulic-capacity table gives combined instantaneous throughput for 'lines 1&2, Dн530mm' in Nm3/hour at various pipeline pressures (e.g. 308,192 Nm3/h at 3.5 MPa, up to 443,392 Nm3/h at 4.6 MPa) -- converting the top of that range (~443 thousand Nm3/h combined) to an annual basis gives roughly 3.9 bcm/y combined, which is directionally consistent with the wiki's stated 3.92 bcm/y total (1.96 each) but depends heavily on which operating-pressure scenario is assumed, so I am not treating it as a clean confirmation of the specific 1.96 figure. Not deleting the existing ref (only a confirmed 404/410 justifies that per standing rules) -- flagging as unresolved instead. FUELSOURCE CAVEAT: GEM's FuelSource='Gazli' (the Uzbek gas field that is the historical origin of the whole Bukhara-Ural mainline, from which this lateral taps at km1385) is plausible given the lateral draws off the Bukhara-Ural trunk, but the wiki's own background section notes the wider Bukhara-Ural system went into partial REVERSE-flow operation in fall 2014 (Gazprom supplying southern Kazakhstan from the Russian end), and this Aktobe lateral's 'Associated infrastructure' is listed as the (domestically-sourced) Zhanazhol-Aktobe Gas Pipeline, raising the possibility gas reaching Aktobe today is partly/mostly domestic Kazakh gas rather than Gazli-origin gas. Could not find a source that states the current gas origin for this specific lateral, so left unresolved rather than fabricating a ref for or against Gazli.
